runtime: Genuine Microsoft XNA 4.0 under Wine/.NET and DXVK 2.6 on private Xwayland

overloads.1: sort mode and four state objects
overloads.2: sort mode, four states and effect
overloads.3: sort mode, four states, effect and matrix

input.source: 1x1 white Color texture over the complete target
input.late_write_mask: ColorWriteChannels.None assigned after Begin and before End
input.factor_case: Source changes from BlendFactor/(173,61,219,255) to InverseBlendFactor/(7,241,19,255) before End; a different device factor is set before End and again after End, followed by Opaque

comparison.details: FNA stores the BlendState class reference at Begin and applies it at End for Deferred. The shipped XNA implementation agrees. CNA previously copied into four value-taking overloads, isolating mutation/disposal and binding a clone. All four now take const BlendState& and use the existing shared-payload assignment.

reproduce: bash tools/xna-oracle/run-sprite-blend-reference-oracle.sh <output-directory>; CNA_XNA40_REFERENCES and CNA_XNA40_WINEPREFIX override the installed references and existing prefix. No Microsoft binary is retained.
regressions: AllOverloads/SpriteBatchBlendReferenceTest.* (five cases for each of four overloads)
WebGPU_SpriteBatch_BlendState late source factor/write-mask and post-End device-state controls
limits: Ordinary RGBA/HiDef on Wine/DXVK. No native Windows, browser, every blend precision/format combination, or physical-platform qualification. Native C++ source-scope retention is an additional CNA regression, not a distinct managed-XNA measurement. C routes keep their copied POD contract; native C++ consumers must rebuild for the signature correction.
